newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Volvo now free to sell P&U stake.
newsitem.headline: Volvo now free to sell P&U stake.

text.p: Swedish automotive group AB Volvo said on Wednesday it was free to sell its 4.7 percent stake in Swedish-U.S. drugs company Pharmacia & Upjohn, but that it has not yet decided it would do so.
"The lock-up period of six months after the sale of the large post in Pharmacia & Upjohn at the end of July expired at the end of January," Jonas Winzell at Volvo Investor Relations told Reuters.
"So now we are free to sell, but no decisions have been made -- otherwise you would have been informed."
He added that Volvo's post in Pharmacia & Upjohn amounted to 19.8 million shares, worth about 5.4 billion crowns.
In July, Volvo sold two-thirds of its 14 percent stake in the pharmaceutical group.
Volvo also intends to sell its stake in Swedish-Norwegian beverage group Pripps-Ringnes, which totals 49 percent, and another six percent of convertibles that Volvo could change for shares.

"We chose to take six percent in convertibles as we did not want to consoldiate Pripps-Ringnes," Winzell said. "The convertibles run over a number of years and before they have expired we will have stepped out of Pripps-Ringnes."
If Volvo would have held more than 50 percent of shares it would have had to consolidate the company in its books.
In the spring of 1995, the value of Volvo's stake in the beverage maker was estimated at just over four billion crowns.
Currently it is harder to value the stake as Coca-Cola decided to end cooperation with the Nordic company, Winzell said.
"But a large part of the value still exists," Winzell said.
